content: Peptic ulcer disease is often indicated by a history of epigastric pain, loss of appetite, and weight loss. These symptoms are highly suggestive of the condition. The most common symptoms of peptic ulcer disease include epigastric pain, which varies depending on the type of ulcer. For gastric ulcers, the pain typically worsens after eating, whereas for duodenal ulcers, the pain tends to improve with food intake. Other frequent symptoms include indigestion, nausea, and vomiting. Patients may also present with hematemesis, which refers to the presence of blood in vomit, or melena, characterized by blood in the stools. Additionally, a loss of appetite and unintentional weight loss are commonly observed in individuals with this condition. It is important to note that a thorough patient history should be obtained, focusing on past medical history, family history, social history (including alcohol consumption, smoking habits, and drug use), and any known allergies.
